papers.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. The active transcriptome, encompassi
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning-based genome annotation and multi-tissue RNA-Seq to characterize the aquaporin, heat shock protein, and LEA gene families in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea, revealing their coordinated transcriptional responses to salt stress. Through phylogenomics and gene regulatory network inference, it identifies synergistic regulatory mechanisms that likely contribute to the plant's salt tolerance, providing a valuable resource for engineering stress resilience in crops.

papers.title: Molecular Systems Architecture of Fibrotic Lung Microenvironment in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Background: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible fibrosing interstitial lung disease characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, disruption of lung architecture, and progressive loss of pulmonary function. IPF is frequently accompanied by comorbid conditions that exacerbate disease progression and negatively impact prognosis. To address the biological complexity of IPF, this study presents a comprehensive molecular systems architecture that enables a system-level understanding of biomolecular interactions within the fibrotic lung microen
papers.summary: This study presents a comprehensive molecular systems architecture of the fibrotic lung microenvironment in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), integrating multi-omics data to map biomolecular interactions. The work provides a system-level view of the disease, potentially revealing new insights into the molecular drivers of fibrosis and comorbidity-associated progression.

papers.title: FERRET: Framework to Evaluate Robustness in Regulatory Networks Using Heterogeneous Cell Types.
papers.abstract: Techniques for evaluating gene regulatory network (GRN) inference methods typically focus on recovering small ground-truth networks or on benchmarking against simulated data. However, both approaches have important limitations and fail to capture the biological variability present in real datasets. FERRET is a framework for benchmarking single-cell GRN inference methods based on a simple biological assumption: independent estimates of the regulatory network from the same cellular state should resemble one another more closely than estimates from distinct cellular states. Rather than relying on
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: FERRET is a new benchmarking framework for single-cell gene regulatory network (GRN) inference methods that evaluates robustness by comparing network estimates from the same versus different cellular states, avoiding reliance on ground-truth networks or simulations. It provides a more biologically relevant way to assess GRN inference performance using real heterogeneous cell type data.

papers.title: Residual-stream geometry of single-cell foundation models carries incremental gene-regulatory signal across tissues.
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models such as scGPT and Geneformer learn rich representations of gene expression programs, but whether these representations encode gene regulatory relationships beyond expression-level confounds remains unclear. Attention patterns in these models have been shown to capture co-expression rather than direct regulation, leaving open the question of whether deeper representations-particularly the residual stream-contain genuine regulatory information.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether single-cell foundation models like scGPT and Geneformer encode gene regulatory information beyond mere co-expression. The authors find that the residual-stream representations of these models carry incremental gene-regulatory signal across tissues, suggesting deeper layers capture regulatory relationships not present in expression-level data alone.

papers.title: A fungal exudate-inspired substrate mixture elicits an emergent growth phenotype and metabolic responses in Pseudomonas putida.
papers.abstract: Microbes in natural environments often encounter diverse mixtures of organic compounds, yet how mixed substrate environments and their molecular composition shape microbial phenotypes remains understudied. Here, we examined how a defined fungal exudate mimic (FEM) mixture influences growth and metabolism in Pseudomonas putida KT2440 compared to individual substrates matched for total carbon and nitrogen. Growth on FEM initiated 2 h earlier than growth on glucose alone and exhibited both the lowest lag and shortest time to maximum biomass compared to individual substrates. Fructose was the only
papers.summary: This study shows that a defined mixture mimicking fungal exudates triggers earlier growth and faster biomass accumulation in Pseudomonas putida compared to individual substrates, despite equal carbon and nitrogen content. The emergent phenotype suggests that substrate diversity itself, not just nutrient quantity, can shape microbial metabolism and growth dynamics.

papers.title: SignifiKANTE: Efficient P-value computation for gene regulatory networks.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are graph-based representations of regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes. Various tools exist to infer GRNs from gene expression data, but since GRN inference itself is already computationally intensive, statistical significance estimates are often omitted. While naïve permutation-based empirical P-value computation methods are relatively straightforward to implement, they are prohibitively expensive when applied to popular regression-based GRN inference methods and realistically sized datasets.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SignifiKANTE, a tool for efficiently computing P-values for gene regulatory networks (GRNs) inferred from gene expression data. It addresses the computational bottleneck of permutation-based significance testing, making it feasible to assess statistical confidence for regression-based GRN inference on realistic datasets.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of single-cell foundation model interpretability: attention-derived edge scores add no incremental value over gene-level features for perturbation-target prediction.
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models such as scGPT and Geneformer are increasingly used for gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, with attention-derived edge scores routinely interpreted as regulatory proxies. Prior benchmarks have evaluated curated-reference recovery but have not systematically tested whether attention adds information beyond expression statistics for predicting the outcomes of genetic perturbations, nor whether attention-identified "regulatory" components are causally required for such predictions. This gap matters because the NLP interpretability literature has established that
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates whether attention-derived edge scores from single-cell foundation models like scGPT and Geneformer provide additional predictive value for perturbation outcomes beyond simple gene-level expression features. The authors find that attention scores add no incremental benefit, suggesting that these interpretability outputs may not be causally informative for regulatory inference.

papers.title: Systems-Level Mapping of the Tumor Microenvironment Reveals Immune-Mediated Mechanisms and Potential Targets in Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic cancer, with limited improvements in patient survival despite targeted therapies and a high recurrence rate (~80%). Current standard-of-care for frontline treatment involves platinum-based chemotherapy, but the emergence of resistant clones limits long-term efficacy. Existing models often overlook critical interactions between cancer cells and their microenvironment. Therefore, we investigated the ovarian cancer microenvironment to identify cell populations and markers driving treatment resistance.
papers.summary: This study maps the tumor microenvironment of platinum-resistant ovarian cancer at a systems level, identifying immune cell populations and markers that drive treatment resistance. The findings reveal immune-mediated mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets, offering new insights into overcoming chemotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Loss of ATP-Dependent Citrate Lyase Drives Left Ventricular Dysfunction by Metabolic Remodeling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic adaptation and maladaptation are hallmarks of the failing heart and may be a target for therapeutic interventions. For example, sustained glucose oxidation during cardiac stress is associated with increased activity and abundance of ACL (ATP-dependent citrate lyase, Acly), which produces acetyl-coenzyme A (CoA) from citrate and CoA and supports de novo lipid synthesis. However, our understanding of how ACL supports cardiac metabolic adaptation and its potential to modulate disease pathophysiology has not yet been investigated.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of ATP-dependent citrate lyase (ACL) in cardiac metabolism and heart failure. The authors find that loss of ACL drives left ventricular dysfunction through metabolic remodeling, suggesting that ACL may be a therapeutic target for heart failure.

papers.title: Systemic trade-offs between core and accessory genomes govern stress adaptation in Rhodococcus erythropolis.
papers.abstract: The genus Rhodococcus is a premier biotechnological chassis for organic pollutant bioremediation and natural product biosynthesis, yet the systemic genetic basis of its stress resilience remains poorly defined. Here, we elucidate adaptive strategies in Rhodococcus erythropolis by integrating pangenomics with multi-omics and phenotypic analyses. We refined R. erythropolis taxonomy using average nucleotide identity across 671 genomes and constructed a high-quality pangenome that exhibits an open architecture, with continuous expansion of the accessory cloud genome via horizontal gene transfer to
papers.summary: This study integrates pangenomics with multi-omics and phenotypic analyses to reveal how Rhodococcus erythropolis balances core and accessory genome functions for stress adaptation. The findings show an open pangenome where accessory genes acquired via horizontal gene transfer drive niche-specific resilience, while core genes maintain essential cellular processes, highlighting systemic trade-offs that govern environmental stress responses.

papers.title: Comparative genomics of the Nap2-2B clade reveals substrate partitioning and niche diversification among uncultured hydrocarbon-degrading Desulfotomaculales.
papers.abstract: Uncultured Nap2-2B bacteria (order Desulfotomaculales; formerly family Peptococcaceae) are frequently detected in methanogenic hydrocarbon-degrading environments, yet their metabolic diversity remains poorly understood. Here, we analysed 17 GTDB r232 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from four genera within this clade. A bac120 phylogeny places Nap2-2B as a monophyletic family-level lineage within Desulfotomaculales. Glycyl radical enzyme phylogeny and operon context reveal strict substrate partitioning: SCADC1-2-3 encodes alkylsuccinate synthase for aliphatic hydrocarbon activation, 46-80 a
papers.summary: This study uses comparative genomics of 17 metagenome-assembled genomes to characterize the metabolic diversity of uncultured Nap2-2B bacteria, a clade within Desulfotomaculales found in hydrocarbon-degrading environments. The authors show that these bacteria exhibit strict substrate partitioning, with different glycyl radical enzymes for activating aliphatic versus aromatic hydrocarbons, and this partitioning correlates with niche diversification across genera.

papers.title: Systems Biology and Experimental Validation Enable Discovery of MMP9-Centered Networks, Anticancer Activity, and Pharmacodynamic Signature in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP9) is involved in extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammation, and metastasis, and its overexpression is associated with poor prognosis in lung cancer. However, the systems-level effects of MMP9 inhibition remain incompletely understood. We combined systems biology with experimental validation to characterize MMP9-centered signaling in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and identify downstream pharmacodynamic biomarkers. Network and pathway analyses revealed extracellular matrix- and inflammation-related interaction modules and prioritized an MMP9-associated ge
papers.summary: This study integrates systems biology approaches with experimental validation to map MMP9-centered signaling networks in non-small cell lung cancer, revealing extracellular matrix and inflammation-related modules and identifying downstream pharmacodynamic biomarkers. The findings provide a network-level understanding of MMP9 inhibition and suggest potential anticancer activity and biomarkers for therapeutic response.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics imputation and embedding with SpaMIE.
papers.abstract: SpaMIE is a deep graph neural network framework designed to tackle the challenge of multi-section integration in spatial multi-omics (SMO) datasets with systematic missing modalities. Current SMO platforms face limitations such as high cost and limited throughput, leading to many large-scale spatial atlases relying on cost-effective mono-omics measurements while only a few sections are profiled with full multi-omics technologies. This results in heterogeneous modality coverage across tissue sections. SpaMIE offers a two-stage solution. In the first stage, it performs spatially informed cross-m
papers.summary: SpaMIE is a deep graph neural network framework that integrates spatial multi-omics data across tissue sections with missing modalities, enabling imputation of absent omics layers and joint embedding of heterogeneous datasets. It addresses the challenge of high-cost multi-omics profiling by leveraging spatially informed cross-modal learning, making it a practical tool for large-scale spatial atlases.

papers.title: Analytical Methods and Application of Single-Cell and Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics in the Study of Ischemic Stroke.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, with complex and heterogeneous pathophysiological processes. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sc/snRNA-seq) has been increasingly applied to investigate cellular heterogeneity at high resolutions.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the analytical methods and applications of single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sc/snRNA-seq) in studying ischemic stroke, highlighting how these technologies reveal cellular heterogeneity and complex pathophysiological processes. It provides an overview of current approaches and their potential to advance understanding of stroke biology.

papers.title: Tensor network-based gene regulatory network inference for single-cell transcriptomic data.
papers.abstract: Deciphering complex gene-gene interactions remains challenging in transcriptomics as traditional methods often miss higher-order and nonlinear dependencies. This study introduces a quantum-inspired framework leveraging tensor networks to optimally map expression data into a lower dimensional representation preserving biological locality. Using quantum mutual information (QMI), a nonparametric measure natural for tensor networks, we quantify gene dependencies and establish statistical significance via permutation testing. From those values, we construct optimal network where genes are positione
papers.summary: This paper introduces a quantum-inspired tensor network framework for inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data. The method captures higher-order and nonlinear gene dependencies using quantum mutual information, outperforming traditional approaches. It provides a new tool for understanding complex gene-gene interactions in single-cell data.

papers.title: Mediterranean Diet and Neurodegenerative Diseases: Recent Advances from the Gut-Immune-Brain Axis to Multi-Omics-Guided Precision Nutrition.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) are regarded as systemic illnesses, mainly characterized by long-term neuroinflammation, metabolic dysregulation and barrier dysfunction. All these factors interact through the gut-immune-brain axis. The Mediterranean diet, rich in plant-based foods, olive oil, and fish, has been consistently associated with slower cognitive decline and reduced risk of neurodegeneration in observational studies and some clinical trials. This review provides a systems-level synthesis that distinguishes itself from previous nar
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent evidence on how the Mediterranean diet influences neurodegenerative diseases through the gut-immune-brain axis, integrating multi-omics approaches to move toward precision nutrition. It highlights the diet's potential to modulate neuroinflammation, metabolic dysregulation, and barrier dysfunction, offering a systems-level perspective for personalized dietary interventions.

papers.title: Matched sampling reveals uncoupled phenotypic plasticity during metastasis formation in uveal melanoma.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is a genetically well-defined yet phenotypically diverse malignancy with a strong predilection for liver metastasis. To define phenotypic divergence during progression, we performed comprehensive gene expression profiling of primary UM (pUM) and metastatic UM (mUM) samples. Two principal molecular subtypes emerged in both entities. Matched pUM-mUM samples showed little transcriptional concordance, indicating extensive reprogramming during metastasis. Approximately half of the pUM samples exhibited a proliferative, MAPK/PI3K-driven phenotype, suggesting heterogeneous depende
papers.summary: This study profiles gene expression in primary and metastatic uveal melanoma, revealing two molecular subtypes in both and showing that matched primary-metastasis pairs have low transcriptional concordance, indicating extensive phenotypic reprogramming during metastasis. The findings suggest that metastatic potential is not fixed early but evolves dynamically, with implications for understanding and treating this cancer.

papers.title: Reference Regulatory Element-Guided Gene Expression Analysis for Mechanistic Inference of Gene Regulatory Networks.
papers.abstract: Regulatory genomics faces a depth-breadth gap: deep multi-omics provides regulatory detail but is difficult to scale, whereas broad expression datasets often lack the regulatory structure needed for mechanistic Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) analysis. We developed Regulatory Elements Guided Analysis (REGA), an interpretable framework that uses reference Regulatory Element (RE) catalogs to infer transcription factor (TF)-RE-gene programs from gene expression data. Across ChIP-seq, knockdown, Hi-C, cis- and trans-eQTL benchmarks, REGA prioritized functional REs, improved RE-gene and TF-gene infer
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces REGA, an interpretable framework that leverages reference regulatory element (RE) catalogs to infer transcription factor (TF)-RE-gene regulatory programs from gene expression data alone. The method bridges the gap between deep multi-omics and broad expression datasets, and benchmarks show it improves functional RE prioritization and TF-gene inference across ChIP-seq, knockdown, Hi-C, and eQTL datasets.

papers.title: Large-scale, interpretable gene regulatory network inference through biologically informed matrix factorization.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how transcription factors coordinate gene expression to establish cellular identity and phenotype. Methods that integrate gene expression with motif-derived regulatory priors and other sources of biological information have substantially advanced gene regulatory network inference by reconstructing condition-specific regulatory architecture. These approaches estimate the evidence supporting regulatory interactions and have proven remarkably successful in a wide range of biological applications. A complementary vie
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a large-scale, interpretable method for gene regulatory network inference using biologically informed matrix factorization. The approach integrates gene expression data with motif-derived regulatory priors to reconstruct condition-specific regulatory architecture, offering a complementary perspective to existing evidence-based methods. It aims to improve scalability and interpretability in GRN inference for diverse biological applications.

papers.title: Transcriptomic profiling combined with pharmacological research of Panax notoginseng-derived nanovesicles for preliminary biocompatibility profiling and STAT5/SOCS3-driven immunomodulation in psoriasis.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease driven by persistent IL-23/Th17 axis activation. While biologics have improved disease control, their clinical use is constrained by immunotoxicity risks and long-term safety concerns. Plant-derived extracellular vesicle-like nanoparticles (EVLNs) are being investigated as a potential biocompatible nanotherapeutic platform, yet systematic safety profiling and network-level elucidation of their immunomodulatory mechanisms remain lacking. This study integrates Systems Pharmacology, computational transcriptomic profiling, and experi
papers.summary: This study investigates Panax notoginseng-derived nanovesicles as a potential biocompatible treatment for psoriasis, combining transcriptomic profiling with pharmacological experiments. The findings suggest these nanovesicles modulate the immune response through STAT5/SOCS3 signaling, offering a safer alternative to current biologics.

papers.title: CoReGRN: a context-aware post-processing framework for gene regulatory network inference revealing regulatory signatures in HIV-Leishmaniasis.
papers.abstract: Accurate inference of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from single-cell gene expression data is challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and variability in gene-gene associations across cells. We propose CoReGRN (Contextual Refinement of Gene Regulatory Networks), a nonparametric, context-aware post-processing framework that refines inferred GRNs by reweighting candidate regulatory interactions using Mutual Information based association strength and local network context. The method uses empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) based scores to assess how unusual each interaction is rel
papers.summary: CoReGRN is a new post-processing framework that improves gene regulatory network inference from single-cell data by reweighting candidate interactions using mutual information and local network context, making the networks more accurate and context-aware. Applied to HIV-Leishmaniasis co-infection data, it revealed regulatory signatures that standard methods miss, demonstrating its utility for studying complex diseases.

papers.title: A multiscale modeling approach to study the role of mechanics and inflammation in the pathophysiology of articular cartilage.
papers.abstract: Mechanical loading regulates chondrocyte health in articular cartilage. While physiological stimuli maintain homeostasis, supra-physiological stimuli from joint injuries disrupt it, leading to osteoarthritis (OA). OA progression involves complex mechanical and biochemical interactions across multiple length scales, which are challenging to investigate experimentally. In silico models provide an effective framework to explore these mechanisms. This study developed an integrated multiscale modeling framework for articular cartilage. It combined finite element (FE) models at tissue and cellular s
papers.summary: This study presents a multiscale computational model integrating tissue- and cell-level finite element analyses to investigate how mechanical loading and inflammation interact in articular cartilage, with implications for osteoarthritis progression. The framework offers an in silico approach to explore complex mechano-biological interactions that are difficult to study experimentally.

papers.title: Hormone-metabolism crosstalk in plants: an integrated signaling network coordinating growth and stress adaptation.
papers.abstract: Plant growth, stress adaptation, and productivity depend on the continuous exchange of information between hormone signaling and metabolic networks. Although major phytohormones have been widely studied through their biosynthesis, receptors, and downstream transcriptional modules, these pathways are still often presented as linear systems. This view does not fully explain how plants integrate carbon status, nutrient availability, redox balance, cellular energy, and developmental signals under changing environments. In this review, we present plant hormone signaling and metabolism as a reciproc
papers.summary: This review argues that plant hormone signaling and metabolism should be viewed as an integrated, reciprocal network rather than linear pathways, highlighting how carbon status, nutrients, redox balance, and energy signals coordinate growth and stress adaptation. It synthesizes current knowledge to propose a more holistic framework for understanding plant responses to changing environments.

papers.title: Causal AI digital twin for bioprocess bottleneck diagnosis via metabolic flexibility and rigidification maps.
papers.abstract: Diagnosing underperforming non-model microbial cultures remains difficult. To address this, we developed an intervention-aware genome-informed digital twin with interpretable flexibility features, explainable learning, and causal-structure discovery to convert sparse anchors into actionable diagnostic artifacts. We grew Stenotrophomonas maltophilia SO-1 aerobically on acetate minimal medium as a controlled testbed and anchored the twin with standardized harvest-time growth phenotypes (OD600 at 32 h). We then generated an intervention-labeled design space via Latin hypercube sampling (LHS), lab
papers.summary: The authors developed a causal AI digital twin that integrates genome-informed metabolic flexibility and rigidification maps to diagnose bottlenecks in underperforming non-model microbial cultures. Using Stenotrophomonas maltophilia as a testbed, the twin converts sparse experimental data into actionable diagnostic insights via explainable learning and causal-structure discovery.

papers.title: SBML level 3 package: flux balance constraints version 3.
papers.abstract: Constraint-based modeling is a well-established modeling methodology used to study biological networks at both the medium-scale and genome-scale. Due to their large size and complexity, such steady-state flux models are typically analyzed using constraint-based optimization techniques, such as Flux Balance Analysis (FBA). The Flux Balance Constraints (FBC) Package extends SBML Level 3 to provide a standardized format for encoding, exchanging, and annotating constraint-based models. It includes support for modeling concepts such as objective functions, flux bounds, and annotation of model compo
papers.summary: This paper describes version 3 of the Flux Balance Constraints (FBC) package for SBML Level 3, which provides a standardized format for encoding, exchanging, and annotating constraint-based models like those used in Flux Balance Analysis (FBA). The package supports key modeling concepts such as objective functions, flux bounds, and component annotations, facilitating interoperability and reproducibility in constraint-based modeling.

papers.title: TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathogenesis extending beyond hemodynamic derangements to involve chronic, maladaptive immune-metabolic crosstalk. Macrophage functional identity has evolved beyond the M1/M2 paradigm toward a model of high heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity, wherein Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) serves as a pivotal molecular hub.
papers.summary: This review discusses the role of TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease, highlighting how macrophage heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity contribute to disease pathogenesis. It positions TREM2 as a key molecular hub in immune-metabolic crosstalk and explores its potential as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how the microbiome, particularly Fusobacterium nucleatum, modulates tumor metabolism and drug responses in colorectal cancer. The model was trained on thousands of drug combination profiles and successfully predicted synergistic therapies, offering a new approach to microbiome-aware cancer treatment design.

papers.title: Longitudinal zone- and cell type-specific pattern-triggered immune responses in Arabidopsis roots.
papers.abstract: Roots, composed of diverse cell types across longitudinal developmental zones, are vital for plant survival against microbial challenges. Leveraging single-cell transcriptomics and live-cell imaging of Arabidopsis roots, we reveal here that plant-derived phytocytokines elicit more potent immune responses than microbe-derived patterns across root cell types and zones. The differential expression of receptors and key signaling modules in distinct cell types and zones contributes to the response intensity to specific elicitors. Phytocytokines sustain growth-defense trade-offs by suppressing the e
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics and live-cell imaging to map pattern-triggered immune responses across cell types and developmental zones in Arabidopsis roots, finding that plant-derived phytocytokines induce stronger immune responses than microbial patterns. The differential expression of receptors and signaling components explains the varying response intensities, and phytocytokines help balance growth and defense trade-offs.

papers.title: CRITERIA: A network decomposition and elementary flux mode translation-based tool for computing equilibria of biochemical systems.
papers.abstract: Analytically deriving equilibria, which often govern the long-term behavior of biochemical reaction networks, is essential for understanding cellular decision-making and robustness, yet remains computationally challenging for large and complex systems. The COMPILES framework of Hernandez et al. addresses this problem via network decomposition but is limited by a computationally intensive translation step and by its restriction to networks with zero kinetic deficiency. We introduce CRITERIA (Computing paRametrized posITive EquilibRIA), a new framework that overcomes these limitations through tw
papers.summary: CRITERIA is a new computational tool that computes equilibria of biochemical reaction networks by decomposing the network and translating elementary flux modes, overcoming limitations of the previous COMPILES framework such as computational intensity and restriction to zero kinetic deficiency. This enables analysis of larger and more complex systems, aiding in understanding cellular decision-making and robustness.

papers.title: From one genome to thousands, and beyond.
papers.abstract: Over the past three decades, Saccharomyces cerevisiae has gone from being the first eukaryote to have its genome fully sequenced to one of the most studied biological systems. Advances in sequencing technologies, functional genomics, and population genomics have expanded the scope of study from a single laboratory reference genome to thousands of natural isolates, and the species-wide pangenome. These advances have revealed vast genetic and structural diversity, shaped by evolution, ecology, and domestication, while large-scale experimental resources have made yeast a model organism of choice
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of Saccharomyces cerevisiae research from the first eukaryotic genome sequence to a species-wide pangenome, highlighting how advances in sequencing and functional genomics have revealed extensive genetic and structural diversity. It emphasizes the role of large-scale experimental resources in establishing yeast as a premier model organism for studying evolution, ecology, and domestication.

papers.title: Biochemical principles of SMAD signaling across the animal kingdom.
papers.abstract: The bone-morphogenetic protein (BMP)-SMAD signal transduction pathway regulates fundamental cellular processes such as fate specification, tissue patterning, and stem cell homeostasis across metazoans and has a conserved signaling architecture. However, the quantitative dynamics of SMAD signaling and regulatory strategies governing pathway activity show a wide range of variation across developmental and stem-cell systems. In the present review, we summarize insights from six major biological contexts-Drosophila embryo, germline stem cells, and the larval and pupal wing discs; the Danio rerio (
papers.summary: This review examines the BMP-SMAD signaling pathway across animal species, highlighting its conserved core architecture but variable quantitative dynamics and regulatory strategies in different developmental and stem-cell contexts. It synthesizes findings from six major biological systems, including Drosophila embryos and wing discs, and zebrafish, to provide a comparative perspective on pathway regulation.

papers.title: A genome-scale metabolic model of a pathosystem sheds light on bacterial wilt.
papers.abstract: During plant infection, complex metabolic interactions occur between the host and the pathogen, including direct competition for resources. While pathogens exploit host-derived nutrients to sustain growth and virulence, plants attempt to restrict pathogen proliferation by limiting nutrient availability. To quantify the contribution of these trophic interactions to disease development, we developed a mathematical model of plant-pathogen metabolism. A genome-scale metabolic model of the pathogen was integrated with a genome-scale, multiorgan metabolic model of the plant and calibrated using expe
papers.summary: This study presents a genome-scale metabolic model integrating both a plant host and a bacterial pathogen to simulate their metabolic interactions during infection. The model was calibrated with experimental data and provides quantitative insights into how nutrient competition and availability influence bacterial wilt disease development.

papers.title: Trans-dimensional Bayesian model averaging for 13C-metabolic flux analysis: Evidence-based flux inference under structural model uncertainty.
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of intracellular metabolic fluxes is central to systems biology and biotechnology. Flux estimation relies on biochemical network models, with 13C-metabolic flux analysis (MFA) being the state-of-the-art approach. However, isotope labeling data are often insufficient to uniquely support a single network formulation. In such cases, flux estimates become model-dependent, highlighting the need for methods that explicitly account for structural uncertainty. Bayesian model averaging provides a principled framework for this purpose, but its application to 13C-MFA has so far be
papers.summary: This paper introduces a trans-dimensional Bayesian model averaging approach for 13C-metabolic flux analysis that explicitly accounts for structural uncertainty in metabolic network models. The method enables evidence-based flux inference when isotope labeling data cannot uniquely support a single network formulation, providing more robust flux estimates.

papers.title: Sex-aware causal inference assessment of the immune system in complex neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: Sex differences, in terms of prevalence, symptoms and disease progression, are established in the aetiology of complex neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease, but the underlying biology driving these differences remains poorly understood. There is emerging evidence from genetic and functional analyses affirming the role of the immune system in such diseases, but a thorough assessment of sex differences in the link between the immune system and neurodegenerative diseases remains lacking. Here, we applied a robust causal i
papers.summary: This study uses causal inference methods to assess sex-specific links between the immune system and complex neurodegenerative diseases (ALS, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's). It finds that immune-related causal effects differ between sexes, highlighting the importance of considering sex in disease mechanisms and potential treatments.

papers.title: WILDkCAT: extract, retrieve, and predict enzyme turnover numbers of constraint-based metabolic models.
papers.abstract: Accurate enzyme turnover numbers are essential for building enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic models. However, collecting and curating these parameters remains a major bottleneck. Indeed, kcat values are scattered across multiple databases, reported under varying experimental conditions, and often missing for many enzymes. To address this challenge, we present WILDkCAT, a Python-based pipeline that enables the retrieval of kcat values from wild-type enzyme measured under user-specified pH and temperature ranges for a given metabolic model. The application to Escherichia coli (iML1515)
papers.summary: WILDkCAT is a new Python pipeline that automatically retrieves enzyme turnover numbers (kcat values) from databases for constraint-based metabolic models, filtering by user-specified pH and temperature conditions. It addresses the bottleneck of manually curating kcat values, which are scattered across databases and often missing. The tool was demonstrated on the E. coli model iML1515, showing its utility for building enzyme-constrained models.

papers.title: Causal intervention validation of gene regulatory signals in scGPT.
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models such as scGPT have been promoted as representations of gene regulation, but their advertised regulatory signal has been judged largely from attention weights, which are correlational. We ask a deliberately bounded question: whether direct interventions on scGPT gene tokens-causal with respect to the model's own computation-recover model-internal transcription-factor (TF)-target dependencies that align with curated references, whether that signal is robust, and whether it transfers to real perturbation responses. We separate these into two explicit validation axes
papers.summary: This study tests whether direct causal interventions on gene tokens in the scGPT single-cell foundation model can recover transcription factor-target gene regulatory dependencies that align with curated references, and whether these signals are robust and transfer to real perturbation responses. The authors find that model-internal regulatory signals can be extracted via causal intervention, but their alignment with known biology and transferability to actual perturbation outcomes are limited, highlighting the need for rigorous validation of regulatory claims in foundation models.

papers.title: Urinary proteomic signature of exercise intolerance in patients at risk of heart failure: evidence from the HOMAGE trial.
papers.abstract: Urinary proteomic profiling (UPP) provides insights in disease mechanisms and origin of symptoms. Using UPP, this study aimed at deepening insight in the biology of exercise tolerance.
papers.summary: This study used urinary proteomic profiling to identify a molecular signature associated with exercise intolerance in patients at risk of heart failure, drawing on data from the HOMAGE trial. The findings reveal protein changes that may reflect underlying biological mechanisms and could serve as biomarkers for early detection or monitoring of functional decline.

papers.title: Aerobic conditioning and ginsenoside modulation modify molecular resilience in middle-aged rats: Differential effects of individual and combined interventions.
papers.abstract: Hippocampal aging is characterized by early cognitive decline, disrupted redox homeostasis, and shifts in amyloid processing. This study evaluated the modulatory effects of aerobic exercise and ginseng supplementation, both individually and concurrently, against these alterations. Middle-aged Wistar rats (n = 30) were allocated into young control, middle-aged control, exercise, ginseng supplementation, and combined intervention groups, and assessed through T-maze and Morris Water Maze tasks. Hippocampal integrity was examined with Cresyl violet staining and Nrf2 protein immunohistochemistry. G
papers.summary: This study in middle-aged rats shows that aerobic exercise and ginseng supplementation, alone or combined, can modulate molecular markers of hippocampal aging, including redox homeostasis and amyloid processing, with differential effects depending on the intervention. The findings suggest potential non-pharmacological strategies to promote brain resilience during aging.

papers.title: Rhizospheric Microbes and Nanoparticles Synergize to Enhance Plant Immune Responses.
papers.abstract: Sustainable crop production increasingly requires innovative strategies that can enhance plant resilience while reducing dependence on synthetic agrochemicals. Recent advances in nanotechnology and rhizosphere microbiome research have created new opportunities to strengthen plant defense systems through integrated biological and material-based approaches. This review introduces the concept of nanobiotic synergies, defined as the strategic combination of engineered or biologically synthesized nanoparticles with beneficial rhizospheric microorganisms to improve plant immunity, stress tolerance,
papers.summary: This review introduces the concept of 'nanobiotic synergies,' where nanoparticles and beneficial rhizosphere microbes are combined to boost plant immunity and stress tolerance, offering a sustainable alternative to synthetic agrochemicals. It highlights recent advances in nanotechnology and microbiome research that enable this integrated approach.

papers.title: Testican-1-MMP axis in tumour extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling: interaction dynamics analysis and an in silico perspective.
papers.abstract: The extracellular matrix (ECM) plays a pivotal role in facilitating tumour development, invasiveness, metastasis, and immunoevasive processes through dynamic ECM remodelling processes. Testican-1 (SPOCK1), an excretory matricellular proteoglycan, is suggested to exert a role in the facilitation of ECM remodelling processes through interacting with matrix metalloproteases (MMPs) and even its less known forms. The structural mechanisms of interactions between testican-1 and MMPs were studied, and their roles in tumour-promotion pathway processes were also examined using a computational approach
papers.summary: This study computationally analyzes the interaction between Testican-1 (SPOCK1) and matrix metalloproteases (MMPs), proposing a mechanistic model for how this interaction drives extracellular matrix remodeling in tumors. The findings suggest that targeting the Testican-1-MMP axis could offer a new therapeutic strategy to inhibit tumor progression and metastasis.

papers.title: Multiomics Analysis Reveals CTHRC1+ CAFs Drive Immunosuppressive Niches and Predict Immunotherapy Resistance in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) orchestrate immune-excluded tumor microenvironment (TME), but the CAF heterogeneity remains incompletely understood in gastric cancer (GC). In this study, we integrated multicohort single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomic data to construct a comprehensive atlas of the GC TME. Unsupervised clustering identified eight transcriptionally distinct CAF subpopulations, among which CTHRC1+ CAFs were selectively enriched in tumors and showed the strongest association with T cell exclusion. Pseudotemporal trajectory ana
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomic data to construct a comprehensive atlas of the gastric cancer tumor microenvironment, identifying eight distinct cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subpopulations. Among these, CTHRC1+ CAFs are selectively enriched in tumors and strongly associated with T cell exclusion, and they predict immunotherapy resistance, suggesting they drive immunosuppressive niches.

papers.title: Metabolic reprogramming orchestrates microglial fate in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury: a spatiotemporal immunometabolic perspective.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a critical pathological cascade that paradoxically exacerbates neurological damage following revascularization therapy for acute ischemic stroke (AIS). The pathogenesis of CIRI is intricately linked to dysregulated neuroinflammation, with microglia-the resident innate immune cells of the central nervous system-serving as central orchestrators of this response. Emerging evidence indicates that microglia undergo profound metabolic reprogramming encompassing glucose metabolism, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, fatty acid metabolism, and NA
papers.summary: This review examines how metabolic reprogramming in microglia—shifts in glucose, TCA cycle, and fatty acid metabolism—drives their inflammatory fate during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). It integrates a spatiotemporal immunometabolic perspective to propose that targeting these metabolic pathways could modulate microglial responses and mitigate post-stroke neuroinflammation. The paper synthesizes current evidence to highlight metabolic checkpoints as potential therapeutic avenues for improving stroke recovery.

papers.title: Uncovering the molecular landscape of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer: A relieff-based feature selection analysis on RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Diffuse Gastric Cancer (DGC) is an aggressive subtype with a poor prognosis and a lack of specific biomarkers, representing a critical unmet need in oncology. This study aimed to elucidate the key molecular drivers of DGC by integrating RNA-seq data with a multi-faceted bioinformatics approach.
papers.summary: This study uses a ReliefF-based feature selection method on RNA-seq data to identify key molecular drivers and potential biomarkers for young-onset diffuse gastric cancer, an aggressive subtype with poor prognosis. The analysis reveals a distinct molecular landscape that may inform future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Integrative precision oncology in neuroblastoma: multi-omics biomarkers, molecular targets, and immunotherapeutic strategies.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma is the most frequent extracranial solid tumor of young children and demonstrates a wide range of biological behavior, from spontaneous regression to highly aggressive metastatic disease. Recent advances in genomics, epigenetics, tumor microenvironment biology, and multi-omics technologies have greatly enhanced understanding of neuroblastoma pathogenesis and enabled the development of precision diagnostic and prognostic approaches. This review examines current evidence for molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying neuroblastoma initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistanc
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent multi-omics findings in neuroblastoma, highlighting how genomic, epigenetic, and tumor microenvironment insights are advancing precision diagnostics and prognostics. It also discusses molecular targets and immunotherapeutic strategies, underscoring the potential for personalized treatment approaches in this pediatric cancer.

papers.title: Radiation-induced network rewiring in cancer: systems-level insights into environmental radioactivity and precision oncology.
papers.abstract: The impact of ionising radiation (IR) from environmental and therapeutic sources is complex and extends beyond the damage to DNA. These perturbations are conveyed by regulatory networks, such as transcription factors, microRNAs, long non-coding RNA, and signaling cascades, which in the end affect the susceptibility, progression, and treatment response to cancer. The traditional reductionist approaches, which are very useful, are not enough to explain emergent properties of these dynamic systems. The system's biology paradigm has a great potential of providing the explanation of the rewiring of
papers.summary: This review discusses how ionizing radiation (IR) from environmental and therapeutic sources rewires cancer regulatory networks, including transcription factors, non-coding RNAs, and signaling cascades. It argues that systems biology approaches are needed to understand the emergent properties of these dynamic networks and their implications for cancer susceptibility, progression, and treatment response.

papers.title: A systems biology approach to find representative genes in Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
papers.abstract: In this study, we modeled gene expression profile data from Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) and healthy cases. At first, the GEO-GSE9476 dataset was processed, and a total of 341 genes were identified as differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in patients, and 599 DEGs in healthy individuals. Gene Ontology and pathway analysis on DEGs led to the identification of 5 Transcription Factors for patients and 3 for healthy cases. Analysis of the respective metabolic pathways revealed a common region in the metabolic pathway between AML and Tuberculosis (TB) that confirmed the validity of our procedure du
papers.summary: This study used a systems biology approach to analyze gene expression data from AML patients and healthy individuals, identifying differentially expressed genes and transcription factors. The authors found a shared metabolic pathway region between AML and Tuberculosis, which they used to validate their analytical approach.
